conviction_note: The commercial lines (Q3 managed inflows of 3.0bn, a record) are already out through the monthly releases, and the sell side has already moved up after them (BofA 2026 EPS +13%, Barclays TP raised, Equita 278m). What the release adds is the Q3 P&L, the NII guide, October inflows and the interim dividend. Nothing I found gives an unpriced number on any of those, so p_up sits at 52. The findings sum to -0.4 because the bar has been raised: the stock is up 5.2% in 5 days on peers' beats, the NII consensus already sits at the top of the guided range, and the interim headline is set against last year's 0.60, which included a 0.20 special. The scaled number is +0.12 because this name's release-day history is mildly positive (6 of 8 up). The two measurements are both close to zero, and the gap between them is noise rather than a view.

already_public.what: September 2026 net inflows: total 1.07bn (best September ever), managed 675m; 9M total 9.52bn, managed 7.24bn (+10% y/y); Q3 managed inflows about 3.0bn, a record quarter
2026 guidance as of H1: managed net inflows about 9bn, NII +15-18% vs 2025 (raised from about 15%), cost/income about 38%, cost of risk about 20bp, DPS above the 2025 base of 0.80
Board date of 10 Nov 2026 for the 30 Sep interim report and the interim dividend
Peer Q3 prints already out: Fineco beat (Q3 net 188.1m, +15.6% y/y, above consensus), Azimut confirmed its guidance; the sector rallied and BMED rose 3.2% on 4 Nov

new_in_release.expect: Q3 net profit against about 274-278m. Slight beat likely (Q3 markets up, record inflows, management fees +15% y/y expected), but the sell side raised estimates in October. Slight up.

The 2026 NII guide (+15-18%). Consensus already sits at or above the top (Intermonte 18.1%, Equita Q3 235m), so a raise is needed just to stand still. A first qualitative 2027 outlook is likely (last year's Q3 release gave one for 2026). Unknown, two-sided.

The 2026 interim dividend. Last year's 0.60 was 0.40 base plus 0.20 special tied to the Mediobanca sale, so a base-only interim would make a smaller headline. Analysts know this. A new special is possible (CET1 22.7%). Unknown.
October 2026 inflows, released with the results as in 2025. Fineco's October was strong (1.7bn), against the BTP Valore retail placement of 16.6bn in October. Unknown, slight risk to managed inflows.

findings.finding: Q3 2026 was a record quarter for managed inflows (about 3.0bn, +49% y/y per Equita). Barclays judges BMED to have had the best Q3 trend among Italian wealth managers in inflows and management fees, and BofA raised 2026 EPS by 13% on higher AUM, NII and performance fees.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On results days with strong commercial data, BMED moved modestly: +2.29% on 6 Nov 2025, +1.97% on 30 Jul 2026, +0.44% on 7 May 2026 (Yahoo daily bars).
findings.original_quote: Analizzando i trend del terzo trimestre, sostiene che Banca Mediolanum abbia mostrato la performance migliore (in termini di flussi in entrata e commissioni di gestione), nonostante altrove si siano riscontrate dinamiche più favorevoli per quanto riguarda il margine di interesse (NII). [Analysing Q3 trends, it argues Banca Mediolanum showed the best performance in inflows and management fees, although NII dynamics were more favourable elsewhere.]
findings.why_not_priced: It largely is priced. The inflows are pre-released monthly, and three brokers raised targets or estimates on them in October and November. If anything were left, it would show up as a consensus still near Equita's 278m with no further upgrades. Instead the stock is up 5.2% in 5 days.
findings.independence: BofA, 15 Oct 2026: Q3 the best quarter ever for managed inflows (https://www.borsaitaliana.it/borsa/notizie/teleborsa/finanza/bofa-fineco-e-mediolaum-top-picks-nella-gestione-patrimoniale-conferma-neutral-su-azimut-107_2026-10-15_TLB.html?lang=it)

findings.finding: Equita models Q3 performance fees at only 12m (against 15m in Q3 2025), while Milan was up about 7% in the quarter. Mediolanum's Q2 performance fees were 39m against 20m expected, so Q3 performance fees could surprise upward.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: H1 2026: Q2 net beat consensus by about 12% on performance fees (39m vs 20m). The stock rose 1.97% on the day and 1.71% the next.
findings.original_quote: Equita stima 12 milioni dai 15 dello stesso periodo del 2025 [Equita estimates 12 million, from 15 in the same period of 2025]
findings.why_not_priced: This rests on an inference from the market's direction to performance fees, so it is weak. BofA's own October upgrade already cites higher performance fees, so part of it is in other estimates. If it were fully priced, the Equita-style estimates would already have moved up.
findings.independence: Websim: Milan headed for a Q3 rise of about 7% (https://www.websim.it/notizie/borsa-oggi/italia/borsa-di-milano-piatta-verso-un-trimestre-in-rialzo-del-7-circa/). Against it, BofA expected negative variable fees at Azimut in Q3. Intermonte on Q2 performance fees: https://www.websim.it/azioni/blue-chip/banca-mediolanum-un-altro-trimestre-con-delivery-molto-solida-20260731072002/

findings.finding: The NII bar already sits at or above the top of the company's +15-18% 2026 guide (Intermonte models 18.1%; Equita models Q3 NII at 235m, above the roughly 218-230m per quarter that the range implies for H2). Merely confirming the guide would read as soft. Barclays notes NII dynamics were better at peers.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: NII guide raised on 30 Jul 2026 (from about 15% to 15-18%): stock +1.97% that day and +1.71% the next.
findings.original_quote: margine da interessi in aumento tra il 15% e il 18% rispetto al precedente esercizio [net interest income up between 15% and 18% on the previous year]
findings.why_not_priced: The market expects a further raise. The risk is that the guide is only confirmed, or that new deposit promotions ('Bonus di benvenuto', liquidity initiatives Intermonte flagged as an NII drag) cap it. If the market had already allowed for a non-raise, the run-up after peers' NII-led beats would not have happened.
findings.independence: Intermonte expects NII growth of 18.1%, at the top of the range, and warns new liquidity initiatives may weigh on NII temporarily (https://www.websim.it/azioni/blue-chip/banca-mediolanum-un-altro-trimestre-con-delivery-molto-solida-20260731072002/). Jefferies says higher rates support NII (https://www.borsaitaliana.it/borsa/notizie/teleborsa/finanza/wealth-management-italiano-jefferies-debolezza-dipende-da-maggiore-costo-del-capitale-proprio-109_2026-10-29_TLB.html?lang=it)

findings.finding: Last November's 0.60 interim was 0.40 base plus a 0.20 special tied to the Mediobanca stake sale, and it was called a positive surprise. The 2026 guide is only 'DPS above the 0.80 base'. A base-only 2026 interim would therefore be a smaller headline than 0.60, which third-party calendars carry as the estimate.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 6 Nov 2025: interim raised to 0.60 from 0.37 including the special; stock +2.29% (FinanzaOnline puts it at about +3% intraday).
findings.original_quote: legato alla cessione della partecipazione in Mediobanca [linked to the sale of the Mediobanca stake]
findings.why_not_priced: Analysts model the base (Intermonte DPS 2026 0.88). Retail-heavy holders and calendar aggregators anchor on 0.60. If the bar had been reset, previews would cite an interim estimate below 0.60, and none I found does. Two-sided: a new special is possible with CET1 at 22.7%.
findings.independence: stockevents.app carries an estimated 0.60 for Nov 2026 (https://stockevents.app/en/event/dividends/40625727, snippet_only). The 2026 DPS guide is from https://www.teleborsa.it/AMP/News/2026/07/30/banca-mediolanum-utile-semestre-16percent-alza-stima-margine-interesse-2026-107.html

findings.finding: The bar was raised into the print by peer read-across: BMED rose 3.2% on 4 Nov with the bank rally and Fineco's beat, and is +5.19% over 5 sessions to 23.70. That is at or above several targets (Jefferies Hold 23.20, Intermonte Neutral 24.3).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Release-day moves since 2025 were small and mostly positive: +0.54, -0.36, +2.55, +1.17, +2.29, 0.00/-1.53, +0.44, +1.97 (Yahoo daily bars).
findings.original_quote: Bene anche MPS, Unicredit (entrambe +3,4%), Banca Mediolanum (+3,2%), Banco BPM (+2,6%) e Mediobanca (+2,4%). [Also good: ... Banca Mediolanum (+3.2%) ...]
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself. The run-up means a modest beat is already in the stock. It agrees with the baseline's run-up lean, so it is small.

findings.finding: October inflows come out with the results. Italian retail took 16.6bn of BTP Valore in October (2026 net retail issuance about 38bn), which Jefferies says pressures fees and deposits, while peer Fineco reported strong October inflows of 1.7bn.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: October 2025 inflows (1.09bn total, 734m managed) were released with Q3 2025, a day the stock rose 2.29%.
findings.original_quote: Il collocamento di 16,6 miliardi di euro di "BTP Valore" a ottobre ha portato il totale delle emissioni di titoli di Stato italiani destinate al segmento retail nel 2026 a 41,7 miliardi di euro. [The October placement of 16.6bn of BTP Valore took 2026 retail government issuance to 41.7bn.]
findings.why_not_priced: This is macro-to-company transmission and a hypothesis. BTP bought inside Mediolanum counts as administered inflow, so the total may be unaffected and only the managed mix at risk. BofA calls the concern excessive.
findings.independence: Fineco October inflows of 1.7bn (https://www.websim.it/azioni/blue-chip/fineco-risultati-del-terzo-trimestre-2026-superiori-alle-aspettative/) cut the other way. BofA calls the BTP Valore concern overdone.

baseline_tension: The findings are roughly neutral to slightly negative because the bar was raised by the 5-day run-up of +5.19% after peers' beats. That agrees with the baseline's small negative run-up lean (-0.15) rather than cutting against it. There is no short anchor (truncated zero).
